and Antalya (Atalia,
Satalia?), that is to say, the western cities to 'Izz al-Din,
and the eastern ones to Rukn al-Din.
However, the magnates of Rukn al-Din did not rest from contention,
and they wished that Rukn al-Din alone should be named Sultan,
and that 'Izz al-Din should be alienated.
Because of this, that Qaratay devised a stratagem,
and he sent word to them:
"Let it be your wish,
and Rukn al-Din is the senior Sultan, according to the command of the Khan which you have with you.
However, arise, bring him,
and come to Aqsarai.
And let 'Izz al-Din also come,
and whatever his brother gives him in love, he will accept."
And when they were persuaded,
and they brought Rukn al-Din and came to Aqsarai,
'Izz al-Din also went out from Iconium to go to Aqsarai {OCR?: 'Uqsarai' in text};
and he placed troops of the Ma'addites in ambush,
and they came from the other side,
and they struck and routed the supporters of Rukn al-Din, and also captured Baha' al-Din his Atabeg.
And 'Izz al-Din took his brother Rukn al-Din,
and did not harm him,
but brought him into Iconium.
And the three brothers sat together upon the throne of his kingdom,
and the coinage was struck with the three names.
And after these things, that is, in the year 1561
of the Greeks
(1250 of our Lord?), the King of France (Roi de France?), one of the inner kings of the Franks, set forth with a great host,
horsemen and foot soldiers,
and legions of valiant men.
And they journeyed by sea in ships and large vessels, which were filled with boundless silver and gold,
and weapons of war,
and provisions.
And the earth was shaken at the report of them,
and it was rumored that they were about to come out against Egypt.
Now al-Malik al-Salih, son of al-Kamil, the lord of Egypt—
the one who, when al-'Adil the Younger his brother died,
rose up in his place over the city of Homs in Palestine—
was waging war to take it from al-Malik al-Ashraf, its lord,
who was descended from Asad al-Din Shirkuh, the uncle of Saladin the Great,
and afterwards Tilbashar was also his.
